Commentary.Commentary: Right, then! That's it from us for this game. New Zealand win and take a 1-0 lead with it. Next game will be crucial for the Windies if they want to stay alive in the 3-match series. Should be a good one given there's a lot at stake. It will take place in Christchurch on the 23rd of December at 1100 local (2200 GMT the previous day). Tune in for that. Till then, cheers!

Kane Williamson says it was a pretty good all-round performance which he's quite happy about. Opines despite there being a below par target to chase, the wicket was a bit tricky so is pleased that his team got over the line. Goes on to state that Doug Bracewell has impressed after coming back from injury and so have George Worker and Todd Astle. When asked about the next game in Christchurch, mentions it's a slightly different surface which has some pace and bounce, so have to adapt to the conditions there. On his break, says he's looking forward to it as he wants to relax.

Jason Holder says it was a tough start and they didn't get enough runs on the board. Adds they lost wickets at crucial stages which never gave them any momentum. States he wants his side to do better in the middle overs and finish well from there. Ends by saying they'll look to do better in the next game in Christchurch.

Doug Bracewell is the Man of the Match. He says it was a good start with the ball and he is delighted to get Gayle. Feels better to get the win. About his knee injury, he says it has been tough but the hard work has paid off. Adds that there is still some niggle but he needs to manage it well.

West Indies didn't have a good enough total on the board to begin with, but some toothless and inconsistent bowling coupled with some defensive captaincy didn't do them much good. Wickets were what they needed but they never did enough to get that. Earlier in the day, a good holding knock from Lewis followed by a brisk one from Powell saw the Windies get close to 250, but that didn't prove to be enough. Stay tuned as the presentation is about to come up...

A rather comfortable win in the end for the Kiwis. They had to chase down a below par total which was made easier by their openers Munro and Worker. Their brisk 108-run stand for the opening wicket pretty much set it all up. But the experienced heads of Williamson and Taylor added a 50-partnership for good measure to ensure their side virtually won the game. The latter stayed till the end and ensured New Zealand got over the finish line.

Wide! Oh, dear... No fifty for Ross Taylor, because Rovman Powell, either cynically, or unintentionally, has bowled it down the leg side. So the umpire signals wide. Even though Taylor misses out on his fifty, he and everyone else will take joy in the fact that NEW ZEALAND WIN BY 5 WICKETS!
Quite full on the stumps, worked through mid-wicket for a double, which means Ross Taylor will have strike and can complete his fifty. He's on 49. Scores are level.
Astle makes room for himself so Holder follows him. Bangs it in short and angles it down, the batsman somehow ducks and evades.
FOUR! Not going to get an easier delivery to put away. Low full toss on the pads, Astle flicks it through backward square leg. Fine leg was in position but he couldn't get to it in time.
Short and wide, the width's there so Todd slashes it behind point. Takes two runs as third man cuts it off.
Full outside off, driven to mid off. No run taken.
Bit short on off, Ross moves inside the line and pulls it through mid-wicket for one run.
Comfortably wristed through mid-wicket. Taylor will come back for the second. 10 to win now from here.
FOUR! Landed on a length around off, Astle slaps this back down the ground. Mid on is a bit wide, so the ball beats him and races away to the boundary line.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Does well to flick it away. Places it comfortably through backward square leg for a run. First ODI runs for Todd Astle.
Astle drives down the ground this time, but the fielder is in the ring for him. So he finds mid on.
Full ball attacking the stumps, Taylor moves across, gets behind the line and drives it to long on for a single.
Rovman Powell to have a go with the ball.
Tests him with another short, into the body. Todd Astle defends it back down the track to end the over. 19 to win off 36.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Stays back and keeps this short of a length ball outside off at bay.
Shorter around off, rises sharply and climbs onto Astle who fends it awkwardly towards backward point.
Todd Astle to bat next.

OUT! Holder gets his second of the game! From around the wicket, Holder lands it on a length outside off. It angles into Nicholls even as he looks to cut. It is too close to play that shot and also there is extra bounce on this one. He ends up nicking it behind to Shai Hope who takes a regulation catch.
Full and outside off, driven towards the cover area.
The batsman plays a pull shot to this short delivery. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Angling into the pads, pushed on the up towards mid on for a single.
Leans forward to this fuller length ball and taps it gently to the covers.
Taylor latches onto this short ball and pulls it over square leg. Hits it in the gap so is able to come back for the second.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Wide! Way outside off, goes across the tramline and so, the umpire signals wide.
Short of a good length well outside off, Nicholls takes a step across before running it down to third man for a single.
Ronsford Beaton returns to the attack.
Moves inside the line and works the slider a bit square on the leg side for one.
Short and around off, Nicholls backs away again, uses his feet well and cuts it past the man at covers for a brace.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Leans ahead and knocks this full ball to cover for one.

FOUR! A boundary almost after 6 overs. Not exactly a sigh of relief for the Black Caps, but it'll definitely speed up the process. Short and wide, slider around off, Nicholls backs away and cracks it through the gap in the covers for a boundary.
Floats it up on the stumps, quite straight in line, wristed just wide of the mid on fielder for a single.
Short and wide outside, cut to the man at point.
Jags back in on off, catches the inside edge and thuds off Taylor's pads. Falls on the off side and Nicholls being alert calls for a quick single.
Keeps a little low as Ross Taylor looks to cut this length ball around off. Misses as the ball whiskers past the off pole.
Short ball cutting away from outside off, Nicholls looks to slap it through the off side but mistimes it towards extra cover. A run is stolen.
Full again, straighter in line this time, eased away in the same region but a single is taken on this occasion.
Fuller length ball on middle and off, driven gently towards the man at wide mid on.
Powerplay 3 signalled. A maximum of 5 fielders are allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the end of the match.
Skidding off the surface, Henry moves across his sticks before punching it towards the leg side.
Straighter one outside off, pushed into the covers.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Nicholls goes downtown as well, plays it to long on for a single.
Full ball which Ross Taylor knocks to long on for one.
Flatter and shorter outside off, Ross chops the cut towards the covers.
Jason Mohammed to bowl now.
Positions himself right behind the line and blocks it out.

That's fallen safely! Henry Nicholls is a lucky man. Short again, on off, Nicholls swivels to pull but gets a bottom edge which lobs behind off his pads. Shai Hope runs inside to try and take it but it falls short of him.
Shorter length angled into the body, Nicholls moves inside the line and works it down towards fine leg for a double.
Tight line on middle and off, not offering much room to Nicholls to work with. Forces him to defend off the back foot.
Length delivery on the off pole, blocked firmly on the leg side, in front of mid-wicket.
Short of a good length outside off, Taylor taps it down a bit square on the off side and calls for the run. Runs and completes it with ease.
Bit slower through the air, drifting in from around off, Nicholls is forward to drive into the covers. Quick run taken. And another too for the overthrow.
Taylor leans ahead, takes it on the full and knocks it down to wide long off for a single.
Quicker and fuller again outside off, pushed to the covers for a single to get off the mark.
Darted full on off stump, pushed back to the bowler off the front foot.
Henry Nicholls walks into the middle next.

OUT! Latham's gone! That's plumb. Full and flat on middle and off, Latham looks to flick but misses. And that becomes his undoing. Right in front of the stumps, needed to get some bat but he didn't and that's that. The umpire has no trouble in raising his finger. The Windies have another thing to smile about.
Sliding in on middle from around the wicket, flicked to backward square leg.
Tap and run stuff from the left-hander. Drops it into the covers and scurries to the other hand. New Zealand just need 48 to win off 78 balls.
Zips off the surface which catches Latham by surprise. He's struck on the thigh pad.
Good length ball angling across, punched to point from inside the crease.
Waits for the ball to come to him, it's on a length and outside off. Taylor guides it down to third man for a single.
Well hit but equally well fielded too. Short of a length ball and it's pulled hard to mid-wicket. The fielder there makes a good diving stop.
Coming back in on middle and leg, worked down to fine leg for a single.
Latham rotates strike by punching it through covers.
Latham keeps this out from the crease.

FOUR! The one thing observed in New Zealand's tour of India is the way Latham handled spin. And again he does well to play this. Nurse drops this short and wide outside off, Latham goes back and cuts it powerfully through backward point for a boundary.
Flicked away off the pads for a single.
For some reason, Chris Gayle hasn't taken the field today after batting.
Latham drives this one through mid on for a single.
This ball is pushed through covers for a run.
Ashley Nurse is back on.
Taylor pushes this down the ground for a quick single.
Short ball on the body, pulled away to fine leg for one.
Places this past backward point towards third man for a single.
This one is pulled away to mid-wicket.
Tom has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
The boundary line at one end of the ground have flown in a bit. Not sure if it is because of the wind or something else. A member of the ground staff is seen trying to put it in place.
Latham keeps this out off the back foot.
Shannon Gabriel has the ball in hand.
Now Latham tucks this down to fine leg for a single.
Outside off, Ross opens the face of the bat to guide it to third man. A run added to the tally.
Short ball on leg, hooked away to fine leg for a single.
This ball is driven past the man at covers for one.
Outside off on a fuller length, bunted towards covers.
Hurled in line of the stumps, hit back towards the bowler.
This ball is glided to third man for one.
Another ball outside off, Rosco finds backward point with the cut.
Taylor slaps it straight to backward point who has a shy at the bowler's end and hits the bull's eye.
Again hurled on the pads, turned away square on the leg side for a single.
Taylor opens the bat face and guides it to third man for a single.
Full ball on middle and leg, Tom turns it through mid-wicket. Before the ball is retrieved, three runs result.
Short ball on the stumps, pulled away for a single.
Latham stays in the crease and defends towards point.
Tom Latham walks in next.

Drinks are on the field now. Windies have been successful in picking up three wickets since the last drinks break. Although it will hardly make any major difference in the final result, there will be belief in the visitors' camp now. Can they trigger a batting collapse from here?

OUT! Holder extracts his revenge! Better late than never. This dismissal has a resemblance of Jason Mohammed's wicket in this. Length delivery angling into the batsman, Williamson tries to be cute by guiding it to third man. The ball climbs more and he ends up chopping it onto the stumps. He is distraught with that. The Kiwis are just 74 away now.
This ball is blocked off the front foot onto the ground.
FOUR! Holder resumes the run-conceding thing now. Serves a gentle short ball on the stumps, Williamson swivels and pulls it through backward square leg for a boundary.
Full ball on off, driven towards covers. A slight misfield there results in a run.
Jason Holder runs in with the ball now.
Another play and a miss. Banged short on the stumps, Williamson misses his pull. Just one run off this over, Beaton is succeeding in keeping the run-flow down, something which Gabriel failed to do.
Back of a length ball around off, pulled away to the man stationed at mid-wicket.
Full ball aimed at the off stick, Williamson defends it off the front foot.
Length ball angling into the batsman, Kane stays back to block.
Finally Taylor gets a run off Beaton after 7 dot balls. Slaps it through backward point to get to the other end.
Taylor hangs on the back foot and blocks.

FOUR! A half-tracker, punished! Nurse knew how bad a delivery this was as soon as he bowled it and he let it know with a grunt. Williamson had ample time to go back and pull it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Nice way to bring up the 50-run partnership between these two.
Taylor gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it to long on for one.
Driven down through mid-wicket for a single.
Pushed back towards the bowler, he gets to his right and puts in the dive to save runs.
Darted around off, blocked with a lunge.
Floated around off, Kane comes down and pushes it back towards the bowler.
Taylor's frustration is evident after this mistimed cover drive finds Nurse in the region. A maiden for Beaton.
In line of the stumps on a length, defended towards mid-wicket.
Full ball outside off, for the drive, Ross obliges with the shot through covers. Nurse gets down to his left to not let the ball pass through him.
Back of a length delivery around off, Taylor hangs on the back foot and presents a straight bat in defense.
Fuller outside off, pushed towards point.
Taylor gets hit on the unmentionables! Beaton hurls it on a length on middle and off, Taylor misses his defensive shot. Wears it on the groin region and goes down in pain. Is good to continue though.
Ronsford Beaton is back on.
This delivery is blocked towards point.
Taylor drives it to long on for one run.
This ball is cut towards backward point.
Taylor has flicked the ball off his pads. They manage to come back for the second.
Williamson goes on the back foot and punches it through the cover region for a single.
Floated outside off, Rosco gets ahead and drives it through wide mid off for a single.
Williamson gets down the track and pats it towards point.
Punched to the man stationed in the cover region.
Ouch! That would be painful. Around off on a shorter length, Taylor goes back to pull. Ends up getting it off his shoulder towards third man for a leg bye.
Worked away through mid-wicket for one run.
Just outside off on a length, Rosco cuts it behind square on the off side for one.
Bowled around off and middle, defended from the crease.
Worked away with the turn towards long on for one.
Taylor has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
This time Rosco cuts this, there is a slight misfield at backward point. This results in a couple. This completes 500 ODI runs for Taylor against the Windies.
Floated outside off, Taylor goes back to cut. But the ball moves in a touch and he ends up being too close to cut.
Well played, Kane! He comes down the track to drive it away but seeing that it isn't for a drive, he just taps it through mid off for a single.
Flat ball in the line of the stumps, Kane goes back and keeps it out to mid-wicket.
Full ball on off, defended off the front foot onto the ground. At the halfway mark, New Zealand stand pretty at 151/2, just 98 runs away from a victory.
Clever cricket. Kane taps it towards mid-wicket and sets off for a run. Lewis fails to gather it on the first go.
Full outside off, Williamson keeps it out from the crease.
Gabriel bowls it short, Taylor has to hop and tap it to the leg side in order to get a run.
Much better. Angles this full on middle and off, Taylor gets a leading edge towards mid off as he looks to work it away.
FOUR! This is not done from Shannon. He just does not seem to learn from his mistakes. Lands this short and wide outside off yet again, Taylor slaps it past backward point for a boundary.
Driven down to long off for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.

A better throw could have had Taylor in trouble. Williamson turns this through backward square leg and hares for the first run. Seeing that the fielder hasn't reached the ball, he gets back for the second. Nurse screams to the fielder to throw it at his end but the man gives in a flighted throw. Nurse is visibly upset.
Flatter outside off, cut to point.
Taylor drives it nicely through the cover region. One run added to his and the team's tally.
Cut away to backward point.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Taylor flicks this away in front of square on the leg side for a single.

FOUR! Gabriel is back and so are the runs for the Kiwis. Overpitches this on off and middle, all Ross has to do is time his straight drive. Does so and Shannon looks to stop it with some cheeky footwork but is unsuccessful in doing so. A boundary results.
On the pads, flicked away round the corner for one.
Full ball on the stumps, Williamson almost play it on.
Wide! Sprayed down the leg side, Kane lets it be. The umpire has to stretch his arms.

FOUR! The extra pace comes in, the ball speeds away with more vigor. Gabriel offers the batsman ample width outside off. It was bowled on a length. Williamson just hangs back and cuts it through backward point for a boundary.
Shannon Gabriel is brought back.
Driven back towards the bowler from the crease.
Williamson drives it square on the off side for a single. NZ require 121 more runs to win.
Rosco has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total.
This pair has been kept quiet by the Windies. Since the time the second wicket has fallen, these two have added only 8 runs in close to 4 overs.
Wide! Fired down the leg side, Taylor fails to get it away. Wide given.
Turned through square leg for a single run.
Fired outside off, Kane lunges forward and defends towards backward point.
Very full flighted ball, hit back towards the bowler.
Taylor turns it towards mid-wicket.
Full and ample width on offer outside off, Ross hits it straight to cover-point.
Slower off cutter aiming at the off and middle stump, Williamson gets an inside edge through backward square leg for one.
Williams seems to be struggling with his hamstring. This could be his last over of this spell.
Fuller outside off, guided through backward point for one.
Slower delivery on off at 106 kph, Taylor is early in his flick. Ends up getting it off the leading edge towards the bowler.
Full ball outside off at 129 kph, Taylor hits this off the front foot towards mid off.
Taylor drives it through wide mid on and ambles to the other end.
Taylor turns it to the man stationed at mid-wicket.
Darted outside off, pushed towards point.
Drives it through mid off and gets to the other end.
Similar delivery cut towards point this time.
Flat delivery well outside off, Williamson looks to cut but misses.
A short delivery which has been pulled away.

A slight confusion between Taylor and Williamson but all's well that ends well. Taylor pats this slower delivery towards covers. Williamson comes down in search of the non-existent run. Is sent back by his partner and eventually makes it in the crease as the fielder fails to collect that.
Short ball around off, pulled away to deep mid-wicket for one.
Length ball outside off, defended towards point.
A slow full toss on middle, clipped towards mid-wicket.
In line of the stumps, flicked away through mid-wicket for two.
Taylor lunges forward and keeps it out with a straight bat.
Ross Taylor walks in at no.4.

OUT! Gone, another one bites the dust! George Worker is the man who has to walk off after looking at ease for so long. Nurse bowls the slider in line of the off stump, Worker goes back to play the cut shot. But the ball doesn't spin away and comes in with the angle. Pegs back the off stump to end the opener's stay. The Windies have hit the right note by sending the two set men back in the hut.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Darted on off, Kane slaps it through covers for a single.
FOUR! Another one! Deft and clever. Flat outside off on a shorter length, Williamson goes deep in the crease and guides it through third man for another boundary.
FOUR! Williamson sets about with the task immediately. Nurse serves it short and wide outside off, Kane goes back and square cuts it through point for a boundary.
Williamson gets going with a drive through mid on.
Flicked away towards mid-wicket.
The Kiwi skipper Kane Williamson strides out with the bat now.

OUT! Oh Munro! What have you done? Just during the drinks break we were thinking which direction will Holder look for wickets and here is one. Williams serves it on a length around off, Munro looks to go over covers to get to his landmark. The ball bounces a touch more and he ends up getting it high on the bat. An easy catch to Nurse at that position is spooned and he doesn't drop this. The delight on Kesrick's face is for everyone to see. The much-needed breakthrough comes in at 108 runs. They still need 141 runs for a win.
This ball is pushed towards mid off.

FOUR! Those who have been watching Munro bat during the India tour would know how strong and productive he is with the pickup shot. Williams bowls it on the pads, Munro moves inside the line and hits it over backward square leg. Goes for a one bounce boundary. He gets to 49 with that.
A full slower delivery at 102 kph, Colin mistimes it towards covers.
Kesrick Williams to bowl now.

Time for some drinks. The Kiwis have set about with their task of achieving a par score in the right earnest. They are in a punishing mood and all the Windies bowlers have taken a beating so far. Holder is searching for options and looking in all directions for a breakthrough. Moreover, there have been three chances which have gone down - all tough ones though. Who'll be the man with the golden arm?
Flatter outside off, cut away through backward point for a single. They thought about a second initially before withdrawing the thought.
This was turned through square leg for one.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
This one is wider outside off, Colin punches it to covers and gets to the other end.
FOUR! Catch it, was the call but not sure for whom. Dropped on a length in line of the off stump, Munro gets down and plays it inside out over mid off for a boundary. He gets to 43 with that.
Darted full on the pads, turned towards mid-wicket for one.
Ashley Nurse is brought into the attack.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
FOUR! He continues on! Short ball and it's pulled away with disdain to send it across the boundary line. There was a man in the deep but even he couldn't do anything with the dive.
Coming back into Munro, he tries working on the leg side but it goes off his thigh pad. A leg bye is taken.
2nd ODI fifty for George Worker! A well-played knock, nicely paced and wonderfully controlled. Short ball angling in, helps the pull behind square leg for one.
Opens the face and dabs it towards backward point.
Short from Holder, George looks to play the ramp shot but can't connect.
Short into the body, pulled away through the vacant square leg area for a single.
Works it towards mid-wicket but doesn't get any run for it.
Short and wide, cracked to deep point to get off strike.
Served on a good length on off, Munro offers a defensive bat in response and gets an inside edge onto his pads.

Run down to third man again for a single. Not sure why Jason Holder doesn't have that gap plugged. Worker likes to play in that area and he's doing it with ease at the moment. Would be smart to maybe have a gully in place and stop those easy singles.
Play and a miss! Back of a length outside off, not much room on this occasion so Worker gets cramped a bit on the cut shot. Subsequently gets beaten as a result.
Camps inside the crease, arches back and glides it to third man for a single.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads.
Hangs back inside his crease to defend with the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Streaky runs but New Zealand will most definitely not mind. Short and wide, Worker throws his bat at it and gets it off the outer half. It runs down to third man and crosses over the rope.
Bouncer outside off, ducked and evaded.
Short of a good length from around the wicket, Worker rises and keeps it out.
Gets behind the line and works it towards short mid-wicket.

Dropped! Another difficult chance though. Would have been an absolute blinder had he taken that. Short and wide outside off, Worker cuts but aerially this time. Kyle Hope (sub) at point dives low to his right, gets a hand on it but can't hold on. It always was dipping on him which made it difficult. A couple taken as the ball rolls behind him.
Full on the stumps, maybe a touch slower in pace, Munro leans ahead and eases it down to long off for a single.
Seaming away from around off, easily run down to third man by Worker for a run.
Length delivery just outside the line of off stump, Worker goes for the cut shot only to connect with thin air.
Angles it across outside off, cut hard but straight to point.
Kesrick Williams to bowl now.
Waits for the ball to come to him, opens the face slightly and runs it down to third man for one.
Munro charges down to this length ball to swing, gets an inside edge through backward square leg for a run.
Shortish ball outside off, slaps the cut to deep point for a run.
Picked that up quite early, which allowed him to duck and leave the bouncer so stylishly. Crouched very low and even held that pose after the ball went past him.
FOUR! Full and wide, begging to be hit, so Worker, being the merciful man that he is, obliges. Bangs it through the covers and sends it all the way to the boundary line.
Comes from around the wicket and pounds it in hard. It's angling in as George Worker takes the pull shot on. The bounce is too steep for him so he can't connect. Good delivery.
Powerplay 2 has been signalled. A maximum of 4 fielders will be allowed outside the ring till the 40th over.

Elegantly done. Worker crouches a bit as he cuts this behind point and takes one. Third man moves to his left and mops it up. Excellent Powerplay for the Black Caps, they're 69 for the loss of nothing at the end of it.

Better. Need to do that more often. Take the width away, cramp 'em for room and start frustrating them. On a length on middle, skids off the deck a bit, Worker gets an inside edge onto his pads as he defends.
FOUR! That's clever batting. Knows third man is placed quite square, so he uses the pace to guide it quite fine through the vacant slip cordon. Amazing, nobody can do anything about that.
Back of a length, it's the slower one, Munro pats it down in front of covers for a quick one.

FOUR! That is bullied! That shot basically says that he's in control and he's not going to let anything get in his way. Munro just stands tall and bludgeons it through cover-point. No stopping that, no chance.
Outside off, played to point.
Length delivery around the off stick, punched to mid off for a quick single.
The batsman guides it to third man. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! Two in two for Worker! He's going along well here. Tad short in the off stump channel, he unleashes the cut shot through point and sends it across the fence.

FOUR! THAT'S CRASHED! What a hit from George Worker. Some room to work with so he crunches it past the diving cover-point fielder for a boundary. The 50-run stand is up between these two. It ends a run of 7 successive ODIs where they have failed to do so.
Moving away from outside off, looks to connect with the willow but gets beaten.
Marginally ahead of a length, on the off stick, kept out with the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Bang goes Munro! Full and right in his slot, he murders this back past the bowler and mid on to beat everybody to the fence. Beaton it seems got his fingers on it as the ball was going past him, so he's gone off the field. Good end to the over for NZ though.
Nice, solid punch from Munro. Just stands tall and hits it square on the off side, only to find the man at point.
Keeps a little low as Worker manages to put bat on ball. It goes off the bottom part behind on the off side for a quick single.
Sees a bit of width offered outside off and goes for it. It's short, he looks to cut but misses.
Just back of a length around off, a solid punch offered to the man at point.
Super shot and an even better save to keep that from the boundary line. Short and angling wide, Worker fiercely cuts this away. Hetmyer at point dives quickly to his right and stops it.
Similar ball, similar defensive shot to end the over.
Rock solid in defense this time. Stands firm inside his crease and blocks it under his nose.
FOUR! That's a beautiful shot. On the up, right off the meat. With his head steady and timing so pure. Drives it down past mid off for a boundary. Nicely done, Colin Munro.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
No ease at all this time around. Comes back in again, on a good length around off, moves past the inside edge of Worker's bat before making its way to the keeper.
Length delivery on middle and off, shaping back in a touch, defended from within the crease with ease.
Jason Holder brings himself on to bowl.
Good thinking from Beaton. Takes some pace off it as he bowls a length ball on middle and leg, Munro backs away and plays it to point.
Wide! Banged in short but it's too short, wide called by the umpire.
Short again, into the body this time, a mistimed pull in front of square leg earns the batsman a single.
Short ball pounded in around off, quite sharp but Worker sees it early and lets it be.
Outside off on a good length, Worker covers the line and lets it be.
Serves it well outside off and it's going away, Worker has nothing to do with it.
FOUR! Superb placement. Sees it angling away, so uses that well to steer it behind point. Beats the man in the deep and starts the over with a boundary.

Just ahead of a length on leg, Colin looks to play the pick-up shot over square leg but misses as the ball goes off his pads on the leg side. Dot ball to end the over, but 16 have come off it. An expensive one for the Windies.
FOUR! Colin Munro is getting a move on here. Has some width on offer outside off, he crashes it powerfully through the cover region to the boundary line.

Dropped but that's a really difficult chance! Really difficult. Full on the stumps, Munro hammers it straight back. Comes to Gabriel like a rocket and he barely has time to react. Gets his hands to it but it bursts right out and goes behind. Two more runs taken.
FOUR! Beautifully timed. Right off the middle of the bat. Just uses the pace so well. Fuller outside off, Munro drives it through the covers for a boundary.

That's a better length from Gabriel. Bit fuller around off, Munro throws his bat at it and edges it over point. Lewis runs back to try and take it but it's just away from his grasp. A brace added to the total.
FOUR! Half-volley on leg stump and Colin Munro eats that for lunch. Flicks it away in style and beats deep backward square leg to the boundary. Nicely hit, but poor delivery.
Good pace and bounce from Ronsford Beaton. Hits the deck hard, bangs it short and keeps it close to off. It's moving off as George Worker withdraws his bat and leaves it alone.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Worker positions himself behind the line and taps it down on the leg side.
Shaping away from around off, Munro glides this down towards third man and earns himself a run.
Nice and straight from Beaton, Munro can only play it back to him.
The physio is out to treat Jason Holder. Maybe a problem with his ankle. Nothing too serious though, the magic spray is out and applied. He seems to fine to continue.
Touch fullish in length on middle and off, blocked with the full face of the bat.
Good movement for Beaton. He lands it on middle and leg, on a length and it moves away. Worker hangs his bat in defense and gets it off the outside edge down towards third man. Single taken.
Places this full ball to the right of mid off and steals a run to keep strike.
Fullish in length and outside off, George with an attempted cover drive which misses.
FOUR! Exquisite! Gabriel errs in line and pays the price for it. On the pads, Worker has no trouble putting this away to the fence with a flick through mid-wicket.
Half-volley outside off, driven and driven hard by George. The off side is packed so he's unable to pierce the gap in the covers.
Makes it go across George Worker, at 144 clicks on a good length, it's left alone.
Fraction straight in line which allows Worker to pick it off his pads and flicks it through backward square leg. Two runs taken.
Lands it on a good length on the fifth stump line, Worker off the toe end plays it towards backward point for a single.

That's gone high in the air but fallen safe! Drags the length ball a touch, on off, Munro swings across the line and lofts it over mid-wicket. Hits it against the wind so it doesn't go across the rope, but it's enough to fetch him three runs.
Brings it in closer this time, but still keeps it full. Munro gets it off the inner half and away on the leg side for a couple of runs.
Maintains a similar length and keeps it outside off, driven again, to mid off. Dot ball.
Goes full again, well outside off, Munro with a mistimed drive which finds the mid off fielder.
Length delivery outside off with some width on offer, Colin Munro looks to smash it through the off side but gets it off the bottom part down on the track.
The debutant Ronsford Beaton to take the second new ball from the other end. Two slips in place for him as well.
Good pace, good length, good line and good carry. Outside off, Worker shoulders his arms to it. Just 2 runs off the first over.
Quite full from Gabriel, on off stump, Worker drives back down the ground towards mid on. No run taken as it's very close to the fielder.
Full and straight on middle and leg, driven straight to the man at mid on.
Second slip has been removed...
In the channel outside off, Worker lets it be. It deviated a lot as Shai Hope was going to collect it. Late swing for Gabriel.
Full again, outside off, driven again but this time in the gap. A couple of runs for Worker and New Zealand to get started.
Starts off with a full delivery angling across, outside off, George Worker looks to drive it through the covers but is beaten.

We are back for the chase. The target is a gettable one for the Black Caps, but a couple of early wickets could make things interesting. Colin Munro and George Worker will open with the bat, while Shannon Gabriel will take the first new ball. Two slips in place for him. Here we go...
